Wierzbica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wierzbica, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Wierzbica persisted despite a formal ban in effect until 1862 - 31 Jews lived there in 1817, rising to 121 a decade later. By 1921, 81 residents identified as Jewish. During the war, roughly 500 Jews from Wierzbica and surrounding areas were confined to a ghetto before deportation to Treblinka in autumn 1942. The cemetery's exact founding is undocumented, though local historian Adam Penkala places it around 1831, likely prompted by a cholera epidemic - notably, it doesn't appear on an 1839 town plan. A 1952 government survey found '80% of stones destroyed'; by the 1960s or 70s the site had become overgrown with trees, and it was reportedly littered by 1983. A symbolic brick gate was built before 1983, and the site is now listed as a protected monument despite having no surviving tombstones.
